explainBack.question: Why doesn't the new $4 input / $20 output token pricing make a Pro subscriber's monthly Claude bill cheaper?
explainBack.answer: Because two separate meters run on two separate billing channels. A Pro subscription charges a flat monthly fee and meters usage as an allowance inside a five-hour window that resets; token prices meter the volume of text processed and are charged per use only to developers who pay Anthropic directly through the API. Changing the per-token rate alters what a developer pays per unit of text, but a subscriber never pays per token, so their bill is untouched — what changed for them is a larger (unquantified) five-hour allowance and a saveable reset.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P005 states the $4/$20 figures are usage charges based on text processed, not monthly subscription prices; P003 defines the subscription meter as an amount per time window with a five-hour reset; P002 and P004 identify the subscriber-side changes as raised limits and a saveable reset.
explainBack.assessment: The article's mechanism fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; both meters and their billing channels are explicit, so a reader could reproduce this reasoning unaided.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A department manager on a Claude Team plan reads a headline about the Opus 5.5 launch, sees '$4 per million input tokens,' and emails finance predicting the team's monthly Claude subscription cost will drop; she also tells staff everyone can now pick Opus 5.5 in the chat model menu.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, which of her two predictions is wrong, which is unproven, and what should she actually do?
unseenTransfer.answer: The cost prediction is wrong: $4/$20 per million tokens is API developer billing based on text processed; the Team plan's flat subscription fee does not price per token, so the announcement changes the team's allowance (a raised five-hour usage limit plus a saveable reset), not the invoice. The selector prediction is unproven: Team is named in the limit-increase sentence, but the announcement supplies no plan-by-plan chat model-selector map, so Opus 5.5 access must be verified. She should check the team's plan details and the model selector in the account itself before telling staff anything.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P005 separates token charges from subscription prices; P002 and P004 name the actual subscriber-side changes; P006 states the announcement does not map ordinary chat access plan by plan and directs readers to their own plan details and selector.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's two-meter model plus its access-boundary caveat resolves this genuinely new scenario cleanly, showing the mechanism transfers beyond the cases the article discusses.
